notes: Card headed 'Re leak & repairs' in blue - the whole card documents an ongoing leak issue and its repairs. Labelled 'No 8 (second side)', 'Contd' - directly continues IMG_5646 (Table Bay arrival)
black = arrival, carried over from IMG_5646
Blue parenthetical '(Lo.) 17/6' - a Lloyd's Agent report citation (London), not a separate port call
black = arrival. NEW PORT (Walvis Bay, South West Africa/Namibia)
Boxed note 'O.H.M.S. / 23.8.42' - the ship went back onto Admiralty requisition (an 'on' date this time rather than the usual 'off' date)

Blue narrative running across this and the next row: '(Glas.)', 'the leak June-July', '...in 29' - describing the leak named in the card's header as first noticed/reported June-July 1942 and continuing into September. Not resolved into discrete dated entries, consistent with how the card frames the whole period

UNCERTAIN - blue parenthetical '(Cape Town) 31/1' sitting amid the September entries. The date doesn't fit this position chronologically (31 Jan is months away); most likely a citation/reference number rather than a real date, left unresolved rather than forced into the sequence
UNCERTAIN date - red = sailing, but the card writes a range '24-25/10' rather than a single day, the same pattern as IMG_5645's Ellesmere Port range. Resolved to the first day

black = arrival, annotated '(prev)' - meaning not established (same unexplained annotation style as the '(PREV)' on IMG_5628 seq 12). NEW PORT (Bougie, Algeria) - timing fits Allied convoy support in the wake of Operation Torch (Nov 1942)
black = arrival, annotated '(abt)' = about/approximate - the clerk flagging this date as an estimate
black = arrival. Year changes to 1943 here, boxed between the reference columns

UNCERTAIN - black = arrival, but no sailing is logged between this and the 19/12/1942 Liverpool arrival above (a month's gap). This may actually be the sailing citation, miscoloured black by the clerk, rather than a fresh arrival - kept as read
black = arrival, date written as a range '28-29/3' like the earlier Loch Ewe and Ellesmere Port ranges

Blue note continuing across this and the next row: 'the damage to tanks & leak in [the] bulkhead' - further detail on the leak named in the card's header, undated precisely but positioned around early May 1943
Entry struck through by the clerk and annotated 'NOT' - voided, not transcribed as a real event
Blue parenthetical '(L.O.) 2/6' - a Lloyd's Agent report citation
Boxed note 'OFF O.H.M.S.' dated 4.6.43 - the ship released from Admiralty requisition. Card ends 'Contd on card No. 9' (not yet identified)
